title: Rukupō and fellow carvers build Te Hau-ki-Tūranga
summary: Raharuhi Rukupō and fellow carvers built Te Hau-ki-Tūranga as a memorial to his elder brother, Te Waaka Māngere.

citations.locator: Final biographical paragraph: meeting house built in 1842–3 in memory of Māngere

claims.text: Raharuhi Rukupō and fellow carvers built Te Hau-ki-Tūranga as a memorial to his elder brother, Te Waaka Māngere.
Te Ara dates the beginning to 1842; NZHistory describes construction in 1842–1843. The interval represents building activity, at year-level precision.
Te Ara describes eighteen expert carvers participating. The house’s collaborative creation is distinct from its later seizure and museum history.

review.corroboration: NZHistory’s 1842–43 account was compared with Te Ara’s 1842 start. Both belong to Manatū Taonga and are not counted as independent institutional corroboration.
